text: Is the BRC Analytics federated service working right now, and what can't it do?
I'll check the BRC Analytics federated service status.

## Abstract

This report addresses an operational question rather than a biological one: whether the BRC Analytics federated MCP service is reachable at the time of query, and what functional limitations it carries. A single health-check tool call was made against the BRC Analytics federation status endpoint. The service reported itself reachable and healthy, running version 0.29.0 in a production environment, with a health timestamp of 2026-09-17T21:27:42Z. The status payload additionally enumerated five documented limitations, each affecting a specific federated tool or endpoint, with a verification date of 2026-09-17. Two of the five concern ENA-related tools that either fail with an HTTP 400 error (`search_ena_keywords`) or silently cap and undercount results (`search_ena`); one concerns a study-lookup endpoint that returns HTTP 500 for every accession; one concerns the scientific scope of the catalog, which holds only genome-computation metadata and two Escherichia coli assemblies with no resistance phenotypes; and one concerns a URL-routing hazard at the MCP endpoint. For each broken or limited component the status payload named a working alternative tool. The result matters because it determines which federated BRC tools can be trusted in downstream analyses and which must be routed around to avoid mistaking an upstream error for a scientific result.

## I. Introduction

**Background.** BRC Analytics is a bioinformatics resource federated into this environment through a public MCP (Model Context Protocol) server. Its tools expose genome assemblies, ENA sequencing-run listings, and workflow-compatibility checks. Because the environment depends on that remote server being online, its availability directly conditions whether the federated BRC tools return real data.

**Literature Review.** No literature was retrieved for this query. This is an infrastructure status check, not a literature search.

**Knowledge Gap.** Before the query, the live reachability and version of the BRC Analytics server were unknown, as was whether any of its federated tools were currently degraded.

**Objective & Hypothesis.** The objective was to determine (a) whether the BRC Analytics federated service is currently reachable and healthy, and (b) what it cannot do. No biological hypothesis applies. The operational expectation was a boolean reachability flag accompanied by a list of documented limitations.

## II. Materials and Methods

**Study Design.** A single diagnostic tool was selected because it is purpose-built to report the live health of the BRC Analytics MCP server together with the known limitations of its federated tools. No other resource was queried, as no other tool reports BRC service status.

**Materials.** BRC Analytics API / MCP server, reached via the `brc_federation_status` tool.

**Procedures.** One tool call was made: `brc_federation_status` with no arguments.

**Statistical Analysis.** No statistics were computed. All reported values are fields copied verbatim from the single tool result: the `reachable` flag, the `health.status` and `version.version` fields, the `health.timestamp`, and the count of entries in the `known_limitations` array (five).

## III. Results

**Data Presentation.**

**Table 1. Service status.**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| MCP URL | https://brc-analytics.org/api/v1/mcp/ |
| Reachable | true |
| Health status | healthy |
| Version | 0.29.0 |
| Environment | production |
| Health timestamp | 2026-09-17T21:27:42Z |

**Table 2. Documented limitations (n = 5).**

| Affected component | Problem reported | Use instead |
|---|---|---|
| `search_ena_keywords` (tool) | Sends an unquoted scientific_name to ENA; ENA answers HTTP 400. The failure is returned as tool text, so it can read like an answer. | `brc_ena_search` |
| `search_ena` (tool) | Caps at 50 rows with `has_more: true`, and never reports a total. | `brc_ena_runs` |
| `/api/v1/ena/study/{accession}` (endpoint) | Answers HTTP 500 for every accession tried. | `brc_ena_study` |
| All catalog tools | Catalog holds no resistance phenotypes and only 2 E. coli assemblies (K-12 MG1655, O157:H7 Sakai). Answers "what can I compute, on which genome", not "how many resistant strains are there". | State plainly; route phenotype questions to BV-BRC or CARD. |
| MCP endpoint itself | The URL without a trailing slash answers 307 to a plain http:// URL; the MCP client refuses the https-to-http downgrade, surfacing as an HTTP error. | Always call the slashed URL. |

**Findings.** The BRC Analytics service is reachable and reports health status "healthy" at version 0.29.0 in a production environment, as of the health timestamp 2026-09-17T21:27:42Z. Five limitations are documented, each with a verification date of 2026-09-17. Two affect ENA-listing tools (`search_ena_keywords`, `search_ena`), one affects a study-lookup endpoint, one is a scientific-scope limitation of the catalog tools, and one is a URL-routing hazard at the MCP endpoint. Every broken or limited component has a named working alternative except the catalog scope limitation, for which the guidance is to route phenotype questions to external resources (BV-BRC or CARD).

## IV. Discussion

**Interpretation.** The objective is met: the service is up, and the limitations are enumerated. The service being "reachable and healthy" applies to the server as a whole; it does not imply every federated tool works, as three of the five limitations describe individual tools or endpoints that fail or undercount.

**Context.** The status payload itself provides the context: three limitations are failure modes best handled by substituting a working tool (`brc_ena_search`, `brc_ena_runs`, `brc_ena_study`), one is a scope boundary (the catalog answers "what can I compute, on which genome," not phenotype questions), and one is an operational rule (always use the trailing-slash URL).

**Limitations.** This report reflects a single point-in-time health check; status can change after the timestamp shown. The limitation list is self-reported by the same service, verified on 2026-09-17, and may not be exhaustive. Two of the flagged failure modes are notable because they can return errors as ordinary text, meaning a raw failure could be mistaken for data if the recommended alternatives are not used.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.** BRC Analytics is operational and safe to use, provided the flagged tools are avoided in favor of their documented substitutes and the catalog is not asked for resistance phenotypes. A sensible next query would exercise a substitute tool on a real target, for example `brc_ena_runs` or `brc_ena_search` for a chosen taxonomy ID, to confirm the ENA path returns data end to end.

## References

[1] BRC Analytics API (MCP server), federation status. https://brc-analytics.org/api/v1/mcp/

## Acknowledgments

Data provider: BRC Analytics (BRC Analytics API, version 0.29.0), accessed via its federated MCP server.
